subject: Helio Health private-offer: renewal, capacity staircase & acceptance path
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Lang <tom.lang@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Helio Health private-offer: renewal, capacity staircase & acceptance path

Tom — thanks again for the time earlier. Per our conversation I’ve attached a PO draft and a short acceptance checklist to make the renewal path as predictable as possible. High-level proposal: 24-month private offer with a staircase capacity ramp (baseline committed units for months 1–3, planned ramp to target capacity by month 6). Key asks from your procurement/legal team so we can finalize:

- Confirmation of the billing cadence you prefer (monthly tranches vs quarterly invoices).
- Procurement contact to receive the DocuSign private-offer (and any PO # you want pre-populated).
- Standard evidence for acceptance (we typically request SOC 2 attestation + usage snapshot + completed acceptance form for marketplace acceptance).

We’re proposing the following acceptance / billing schedule (draft):
- Countersign by 2028-02-22 (DocuSign link to follow).
- Month 1 invoice to kick on contract effective date; acceptance evidence due within 30 days of go-live window.
- If Helio requires staged invoicing, we can split into up to 3 tranches aligned to fiscal quarter.

I attached Helio_PO_Draft_v3.pdf (contains the 24mo pricing matrix + proposed SLA tier) and the evidence checklist for legal/IT. Ben and Soojin are on copy and are coordinating the private-offer paperwork and evidence pack.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm procurement contact and preferred billing cadence.
2) If the PO needs redlines, send to ben_carter@redwood.ai (he’ll coordinate with legal).
3) We’ll send the DocuSign private-offer and the HubSpot deal will be updated with the accepted PO and invoice schedule.

Thanks — look forward to getting this across the finish line.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Manager, Marketplace Sales — Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference
From: Tom Lang <tom.lang@heliohealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Feb 2028 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Helio Health private-offer: renewal, capacity staircase & acceptance path

Naomi — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifying items from our side:

- Procurement contact will be Maya Patel (maya.patel@heliohealth.com). Please include her on all sending.
- Helio prefers quarterly invoicing where possible — can you confirm whether Redwood can issue 3 invoices per year aligned to our fiscal quarters for the 24mo term?
- On acceptance evidence: SOC 2 Type II is fine, but legal also requests a short statement of data handling for the private deployment (who has access to logs / retention period). Can your security team supply that?

We’ll review the PO draft and get Maya’s team to jump in on redlines if needed. Also please send the DocuSign link when ready; we’ll aim to countersign within the week if terms align.

—Tom
Tom Lang
Head of Procurement, Helio Health

Naomi / Soojin — quick internal note and recommended execution checklist before we send DocuSign: 

1) Pricing matrix: the attached PO draft (v3) uses a 10% blended tier discount for months 7–24 once Helio hits the target capacity threshold. If Helio requests quarterly invoices, we’ll need to map the tranches to their FY quarters. Recommend we propose 3 invoices per year (Feb/May/Aug) for year 1 and continue cadence for year 2; that aligns with their ask and reduces AP friction.

2) Evidence pack: we should require SOC2 Type II report, a completed acceptance form (we have a short single-sheet), and a first-month usage snapshot from the onboarding team. I’m attaching a focused evidence-checklist.xlsx we can send to Helio procurement.

3) Security note: legal will need a short data-handling statement for private deployment (retention windows, log access). Soojin — can you pull the standard one-pager we use for private customers and add to the evidence packet?

4) Redlines: if Helio’s procurement sends redlines, route to me first and I’ll triage with legal (lee_legal@redwood.ai). For any SLA exceptions we’ll document an SLA appendix in the PO.

5) HubSpot / deal: update DEAL-11829 with the tranche preference and add Maya Patel as primary procurement contact. I’ll log the invoice plan in the internal checklist.

I’ll be available for a quick call with Maya if helpful — suggest we wait for Tom/Maya to confirm DocuSign cadence and then finalize.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Marketplace Partnerships — Redwood Inference

Subject: Final: DocuSign link + acceptance checklist (Helio Health private offer)

Tom / Maya — following up with final next steps and the DocuSign envelope. Thanks for confirming procurement contact, Tom.

Confirmed items:
- Billing cadence: Redwood can support quarterly invoicing. For ease we’ve proposed 3 invoices per year aligned to your quarters (Feb/May/Aug). If you want a different mapping for year 2 we can adjust before countersignature.
- Evidence: SOC2 Type II + completed acceptance form + first-month usage snapshot. Soojin is attaching the standard one-pager on data handling for private deployments (retention, log access, KMS integration notes).
- DocuSign: https://docusign.com/heliopo/DEAL-11829 (private-offer envelope). Please review and countersign by 2028-02-22 to keep the proposed ramp timeline.
- Invoicing: first invoice will be due on the contract effective date. If Helio elects split tranches we’ll include invoice schedule in the PO.

Attachments: Helio_PO_Draft_v3.pdf; evidence-checklist.xlsx.

If Maya’s team needs a short 15-min sync I can set that up early next week. Ben — please share the evidence-checklist.xlsx to Maya and add the data-handling one-pager when you send.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to getting this into effect.

Best,
